# sesam.yml can be rebuilt from .sesam, so a missing one is a damaged repo, not
# none at all: the hook must still guard .sesam instead of stepping aside.

sesam-repo admin a.txt b.txt
exec sesam hook install

cp $TMPDIR/a.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'one'
cp $TMPDIR/b.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'two'

# Roll back the log and drop sesam.yml: the hook still refuses.
exec git checkout HEAD^ -- .sesam
rm sesam.yml
exec git add -A
! exec git commit -m 'oops'
stderr 'is not a prefix of the staged changes'
exec git log --oneline
! stdout 'oops'

# init on the half repo re-runs setup and points at the way back.
exec git checkout HEAD -- .sesam
exec sesam init
stdout 'sesam.yml is missing - run `sesam config reset --force`'
exec sesam config reset --force
exists sesam.yml

# Without the vault (git rm leaves ignored leftovers in .sesam), setup refuses
# instead of sending you back to init.
exec git rm -q -r .sesam
! exec sesam init
stderr 'no audit log at'
stderr 'git checkout HEAD -- .*\.sesam'

# Following the advice gets the vault back as it was.
exec git checkout HEAD -- $WORK/.sesam
exec sesam verify --all

-- a.txt --
A
-- b.txt --
B
